oluminescence spectrum of the nanobeam waveguide from 1260 to 1500 nm

wavelength range using the same measurement setup (Figure S4(a)). We observed a strong peak

at 1277 nm corresponding to the zero-phonon line of the silicon G centers. Furthermore, we found

another characteristic E-line emission at 1381 nm, which is attributed to a local vibration mode of

the G center [1] . The presence of the E-line further supports the conclusion that the collected emission

is from silicon G centers.

Figure S4(b) shows the zero-phonon line of the G center ensemble at high excitation laser power.

We fitted the spectrum data using Gaussian function and achieved a spectral linewidth of 1.28 nm

(red solid line). This linewidth is comparable to other reported inhomogeneous broadening values

in the range of 1.1-1.3 nm for similar G centers [2,3] .

Figure S4. Photoluminescence spectra of G center ensemble in a nanobeam waveguide. (a) Wide

range photoluminescence spectrum in log scale. Yellow and green boxes are the zero-phonon line

(1277 nm) and E-line (1381 nm) of the G center ensemble. (b) Photoluminescence spectrum at

high excitation laser power (black line) and its Gaussian fitting (red line) with a linewidth of 1.28

nm.
